length.text: About 56 to 107 cm; record about 159 cm

overview.text: The Banded (or Southern) Water Snake is a harmless, mostly aquatic snake of the south-eastern United States.

identification.text: Grey, greenish-grey or brown with dark crossbands, a flat head and a fairly heavy body; many are so dark the pattern hardly shows. The belly is off-white.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 56 to 107 cm long; the record, a Florida snake, was about 159 cm (62.5 in).

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: From southern Illinois south to Louisiana and east to North Carolina and Florida.

distribution.label: Introduced
distribution.text: Introduced populations live in California (over 300 were caught around Los Angeles in 2009) and other places.

habitat.text: Almost any fresh water - lakes, marshes, ponds and streams - staying among plants along the shore.

behaviour.text: Active by day and by night; it basks on logs and branches over the water or forages in the shallows.

diet.text: Mainly fish and frogs; young ones eat mostly fish and switch to frogs as they grow.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to about 15 to 20 live young in summer.

recognise.text: Dark crossbands on a grey or brown body.
Usually in or near fresh water.
